details: CONFIRMED by reproduction. take_worktree_lock writes os.getpid() of relay into the lock file; since pass_fds hands the lock
to the command so that it outlives relay (review F4 of the design), the holder after a SIGKILL is the command, whose pid is
never written. The design promised the line names the holder ("the holder writes its pid into the file") and relies on it
for the only recovery it offers (an orphan that hangs forever "makes the next gate wait with the line above naming its
pid ... a hung real gate is killed by hand"). test_t3 checks only the line's prefix, so the wrong pid passes. The same gap
makes a detached daemon that a gate command starts (setsid, inheriting the fd from bash) block every later gate of the
worktree forever while the line names a finished relay (see F2). Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: scratchpad/repro/test_deadpid.py (Slots fixture, N=2: start A, wait for started, A.kill(), start B, read B's line):
LINE: gate: waiting for the gate already running in this worktree (pid 78317) named pid alive: False relay pid: 78317 command pid: 78465
lib/relay_gate.py:137 handle.write("%d\n" % os.getpid())  -- the only pid ever written
tests/test_gate_slots.py:344 assertRegex(line, r"^gate: waiting for the gate already running in this worktree")  -- pid not checked
failing_case: Gate A runs in worktree x; A's `relay gate` process (pid 78317) is killed with SIGKILL while its command (pid 78465, own
session) runs on. Gate B in x prints "gate: waiting for the gate already running in this worktree (pid 78317)" and waits
without a time limit. pid 78317 no longer exists, so a person who follows the design's "a hung real gate is killed by
hand" kills nothing ("no such process") and B waits on. It should name a process that is alive and holds the lock: the
fix_hint: After Popen, rewrite the lock file as "<relay pid> <command pid>" (the command's pid is its process group, start_new_session);
in take_worktree_lock's waiting line name the live one ("pid 78317, command group 78465", or only the group when the relay
pid is gone). Extend test_t3 to assert the named pid is alive.
pass_cases: 1. A killed with SIGKILL while its command runs; B in the same worktree: the waiting line names the command's pid/process
group (78465 in the run above), and `os.kill(<named pid>, 0)` succeeds while B waits.
2. A alive and running (T1): the waiting line still names A's relay pid (first.pid), as test_t1 asserts today.
3. After the orphan ends, B runs (T3, 2 runs) and its line or the lock file names B's own pid.
4. A killed after its command ended: B prints no waiting line and runs (test_t3_a_killed_gate_whose_command_has_ended).
reason: tests/test_gate_slots.py test_f1 (line ~255) asserts the named pid is the command group and alive; fails at 595d55f, passes at head.
findings.summary: after a SIGKILLed gate the waiting line names the dead relay pid, not the orphaned command that holds the lock

details: PLAUSIBLE (not reproduced; relay's own bin/ci starts no detached process: the only start_new_session in its tests is
Python's Popen, which closes inherited fds). Traced: Popen(pass_fds=(lock.fileno(),)) clears close-on-exec on the fd in the
command; bash and the programs it starts keep inherited fds; only processes in the command's group are killed. The design
accepted an unbounded wait for an orphan that hangs, but a daemon is not a hung gate and cannot be found from the line.
Low because no relay project is known to start such a daemon today; cheap once F1 records the command's group (the waiter
can see that the recorded group is empty and say a stray process holds the lock). Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: plugins/core/tests/merge.test.sh:243 subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True)  (Python: close_fds, no inheritance)
lib/relay_gate.py:124-125 Popen(..., start_new_session=True, pass_fds=(lock.fileno(),)); finally: os.killpg(proc.pid, SIGKILL)
failing_case: A project's gate command (bash) starts a background server that calls setsid (an sccache server, a git fsmonitor daemon, a
test helper with its own session) and lives on. bash passes the inherited lock fd to it; killpg at the end of the gate does
not reach it (another process group). Every later `relay gate` in that worktree prints the waiting line naming the
finished relay pid and waits forever. Before this change it ran. It should either not block, or say what holds the lock
fix_hint: With the command's pgid in the lock file (F1): when the lock is busy, the recorded relay pid is dead and os.killpg(pgid, 0)
says the group is gone, print "gate: the worktree lock is held by a process outside the last gate (lsof <path>)" once.
pass_cases: 1. A gate command `(setsid sleep 600 &) ; exit 0` finishes; a second gate on a new commit of that worktree either runs, or
prints within 1 s a line that names the lock file and that the holder is outside the gate's process group.
2. T3 (orphaned command after SIGKILL of relay) still blocks the next gate until the orphan ends.
3. T1 (second gate while the first runs) still waits and reuses the first log.

findings.summary: a process the gate command detaches (setsid) inherits the lock fd and blocks every later gate of the worktree with no bound
